title: kb_ask.py, a status: hook prefix and one AGENTS.md line send status questions to kbmon --status first
goal: mon_status.topic_of(question) maps a status question to its topic by fixed cue words or gives None, so a docs question about sessions, cost or status stays a lookup; kb_ask.py answers a question topic_of maps by running kbmon.py --status TOPIC before any pack or model, its --route printing the plan kind status; the kb hook blocks a status: prompt with the status answer as the reason (no model tokens) while a status+: prompt goes through with the answer as context; AGENTS.md carries one line that sends status questions to kbmon.py --status first and asks for results in plain words, not backlog ids, within its 4096-byte cap

a new skill instead, AGENTS.md unchanged: 4091 bytes

notes: Plan 2026-10-19: premise: no _tools/mon_status.py, and kb_hook.py --test 'status: how much did today cost' gives no output. The recommended rule answer's AGENTS.md line, measured at 4085 bytes on the base (measure again after ST-qpcva3jl, which also touches AGENTS.md): '- Status (sprints, sessions, load, cost): `python3 _tools/kbmon.py --status [TOPIC]`; results, not backlog ids. Hooks `kb:`, `status:` answer; `kb+:`, `status+:` pass on.' in place of the kb: hook line, with the Skills paragraph's links note dropped. A status: prompt whose kbmon run fails or times out goes through with a note of what failed, as backlog: does. The check keeps docs questions (Claude Code sessions, an Intune licence cost, GPO processing order, a ConfigMgr deployment status) as lookups.
